blocks.text: Every match is different
A system keeps its star, signature feature and character, but its seed reshuffles the details. Pick the same system and seed to replay a map exactly; both players always get the same layout.
•  Worlds and belts: one more or fewer than the system's usual count
•  Belt shape: spread, density, arc length and thickness; where the home belts sit
•  Belt richness: how many big rocks each belt has
•  Planet positions and moons: where every world sits.
•  Spice nebulae: size, distance, angle, and sometimes how many clouds
•  Debris ring: size, thickness.
•  Twin suns: orbit size and speed (the safe lane moves differently)
•  Ion storms: size, drift speed and path
Orion Reach
The even, open classic.
Spice nebulae: one cloud on each flank, equally far from both bases, in the contested middle.
How it plays: The even, open map. Both flank clouds lie as close to the enemy as to you, so the spice goes to whoever holds the middle.
Vega Drift
Balanced worlds around twin suns.
Star: twin White Star.
Twin suns: two radiation zones circle the center, and the safe lane between them keeps moving.
Spice nebulae: two arcs of gas across the lane between the bases, just outside the suns' orbit.
How it plays: The suns' radiation sweeps the center, so the lane between the bases opens and closes, and the spice bands lie right across it.
Kharon Expanse
Sparse and spice-rich.
Spice nebula: a full ring of gas around the star, seeded with extra spice rocks, on top of a third of all rocks being spice.

How it plays: Few worlds, but the richest spice anywhere: about a third of its rocks, plus a wide ring of gas around the star. That gas carries low Radiation, so shields stay down inside it and fights there grind on.
Tethys Cluster
Crowded worlds behind a debris ring.
Debris ring: an impassable wall of rubble broken by a few narrow gaps (how many varies by seed), each one a chokepoint. Two worlds per player, of any rocky type and size, lie inside it.
Spice nebulae: a few small clouds scattered outside the debris ring, near the outer worlds.
How it plays: The inner worlds sit behind the debris ring, reachable only through its gaps. Hold a gap and you hold the inner system; the outer pockets offer easy, safe spice.
Sable Verge
Heavy belts, swept by ion storms.
Ion storms: ragged clouds of charged gas drift through the system, crackling with lightning.
Spice nebulae: a great cloud on each base's flank, your own to harvest and the enemy's to raid.

How it plays: Heavy belts and sparse worlds make it a mining race. Ion storms slow, blind and burn anything they catch, knocking its shields offline, and each side's spice cloud is an inviting raid target.
Silent Void
No hazards: no nebulae, storms or rings.
How it plays: Nothing in the way and nowhere to hide: no nebulae, storms or rings, only the star's own zone. Spice comes only from rocks and Spice Extractors, and fleets meet in the open.
Uncharted Space
A new system every match.
Everything is drawn fresh from the match's seed, and the same seed always gives the same system:

- Suns: one, two or three, each any type, Red Dwarf to Blue Giant.
- Hazard: none, a debris ring, ion storms or a spice ring, equally likely.
- Spice nebulae: one of four layouts.
How it plays: nothing about the map is known in advance, so whoever scouts first is first to know where the worlds and gas lie.
